role: Domain 2 R1-verify (zombie competition and zombie mimics)

mechanism.code: rev0 A startup: push cs/pop es (ES=arena), DI=0 (initial), DF=0; mov ax,0F2E2h; mov dx,0C381h; mov bx,026FFh; mov cx,04A17h; int 087h -> the FIRST occurrence of E2 F2 81 C3 scanning forward from 1000:0000 is replaced by FF 26 17 4A (jmp [4A17h] = B zombie_entry). One INT 87h charge, no location feedback (Cpu.int87 in repos/corewars8086-6.0.0).
mechanism.zom20a: live loop 001F-002C, target window at +2Bh (loop 001Fh = E2 F2, followed by 81 C3).
mechanism.mimics: E2 F2 81 C3 also at HRZ_Grindo_Holics1+33h (exact copy of zom20a 001F-0044 in dead code, entry jumps to 56h), HRZ_Grindo_Holics2+45h and +1C5h (dead code, entry jumps to 60h), GSA_callfart1+46h, GSA_callfart2+04h (dead data behind jmp 2Ch). AVI_AnotherBitInTheWall has only 41 93 E2 F2 (not a decoy for rev0's pattern). Every 4-byte window of zom20a occurs in Grindo1/Grindo2, so no other INT 87h pattern can avoid Grindo's decoys.
mechanism.chain: zom20b/d have CX=0 and four identical EB F9 CC CC tails at +11Ah,+133h,+14Ch,+165h; the live one is +14Ch (entry jmp 139h). B's own backward INT 87h hits the dead top copy +165h; the live tail is reached only by the second backward search run by a captured zom20a (CX!=0 path). So a missed zom20a capture also loses the b/d capture (hypothesis consistent with the null effect of fixB).

threatFindings.threat: Zombie mimics (Grindo1/2, callfart1/2) absorb rev0 A's single forward INT 87h (E2 F2 81 C3) when loaded below zom20a
A 14-byte INT 86h planter of E2 F2 81 C3 at 1000:0000 removes the capture completely
b/d capture depends on the zom20a capture, so a mimic breaks the whole chain
AVI_AnotherBitInTheWall acts as a zom20a decoy for rev0
Grindo2 takes zom20b directly by address ([2612h] + xlat table at +0ACh, E9 jmp patch), competing with our chain

recommendation: Do not promote fixB (screen ALL +0.0035, no effect on its threat). Report the weakness as verified: the zom20a capture (worth about 0.13-0.22 points per battle in 2025-Zombie cohorts) is a single point of failure. Present zom20a mimics already remove about 0.1-0.15 of it in Grindo/callfart cohorts, and a trivial planter removes all of it. Untested fix ideas for R4: (1) A searches backward (std), which beats low-address planters but not random mimics; (2) let B's own INT 87h search for zom20a backward when A searches forward, so zom20a is missed only if decoys sit on both sides (cost: B no longer burns the dead top b/d tail +165h, so the b/d chain must be checked); (3) any fix must keep the zom20a -> b/d chain intact.
